name: Excavated (a ground face left as it was dug)
process: A shaft is dug through the ground and its face left as the tools leave it: the made ground (hardcore, crushed stone tipped and rolled) crumbles out between its stones; topsoil and subsoil crumble; the stiff clay-with-flints is cut smooth by the spade and keeps its marks; the chalk breaks blocky along its bedding and joints; the flints in it break conchoidally; the fossils' moulds are stained by the iron that replaced their shells. Each layer is its own substance, and the working lays it: one working per layer (excavated.<layer>), as the Cube's sheet names them.

layers.text: Under the site: hardcore -0.510 to -0.720; topsoil to -1.020; subsoil to -1.500; clay-with-flints to -4.000 (a solution pipe to -4.750); chalk below, with flint bands at -4.580 and -5.360 and an ammonite and an urchin.

faces.text: Crushed stone: angular stones 12 to 28 mm, up to 14 mm proud. Topsoil and subsoil: crumbly, relief 7 mm and 4 mm. Clay-with-flints: smooth, spade-cut, vertical marks 1.8 mm deep at a 0.11 pitch. Chalk: blocky, relief 10 mm and 5 mm, bedding partings every 0.37, 5 mm deep.

descriptions.text: Soils and rocks are described in the field by their colour (Munsell notation), consistency and structure; chalk by its grade of weathering and its discontinuities.
descriptions.source: BS 5930:2015+A1:2020, Code of practice for ground investigations, section 6; J. M. Hodgson (ed.), Soil Survey Field Handbook, Soil Survey Technical Monograph 5 (1997)

unverified.reason: No sample of the site's own ground was measured: each layer's colour is a first value from the Munsell notation field descriptions give it.

sources: BS 5930:2015+A1:2020, Code of practice for ground investigations
J. M. Hodgson (ed.), Soil Survey Field Handbook (1997)
R. A. Downing, M. Price and G. P. Jones (eds.), The Hydrogeology of the Chalk of North-West Europe (Oxford, 1993)
